Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:1.hebrew: המבכרת המקשה לילד - בפטר רחם שלה, מותר לחתוך אבר אבר כשהוא יוצא ראשון ראשון:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:1.english: An animal giving birth for the first time that encounters difficulty giving birth - with her firstborn [lit., opener of her womb], it is permitted to cut [the fetus] limb by limb as it emerges, one by one:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:2.english: And casts [it] to the dogs - for as long as its majority has not emerged, it is not consecrated:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:3.english: [If] a majority of it emerged - all at once, and he cut it [up]:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:4.hebrew: ה"ז יקבר - דביציאת הרוב חלה קדושה עליו, דקרינא ביה "אשר יולד":
Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:4.english: It must be buried - For upon the emergence of the majority [of the fetus], sanctity takes effect upon it, since we apply to it [the verse], "that is born":

Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:5.hebrew: ופטורה מן הבכורה - שהבא אחריו אינו בכור, בין שיצא ראשון אבר אבר ובין שיצא רוב כאחת, דהא שני לאו פטר רחם הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:10:5.english: And [she is] exempt from [the law of] the firstborn - [meaning] that the [offspring] that comes after it is not a firstborn, whether the first emerged limb by limb or whether a majority emerged at once, since the second is not [that which] opens the womb:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:11:1.english: And then another one-third emerged - And behold, here is a majority [of the fetus]:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:11:2.hebrew: רב הונא אמר קדוש - בכור זה, וקרב לגבי מזבח וניתן לכהן:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:11:2.english: Rav Huna says [it is] consecrated - this firstborn, and it is offered upon the altar and given to a priest:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:11:3.hebrew: אינו קדוש - והרי הוא חולין, כדמפרשי טעמייהו:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:11:3.english: [It is] not consecrated - and behold, it is non-sacred [chullin], as they explain their reasons:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:12:1.hebrew: למפרע הוא קדוש - אע"ג דבלידה תלא רחמנא וברובא הוא דהויא לידה, מיהו כי נפיק רובא משוי ליה לידה מתחלה, ואגלאי מלתא דכי זבין לעובד כוכבים לאו כלום זבין, דאין לו חלק בו:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:12:1.english: It is consecrated retroactively - Even though the Merciful One made [consecration] dependent on birth, and birth occurs [only] with [the emergence of] the majority [of the animal], nevertheless, when the majority emerges, it renders it a birth from the outset, and it is revealed that when he sold [it] to a gentile, he sold nothing, for he has no share in it:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:13:1.hebrew: מכאן ולהבא - מיציאת רוב ואילך הוא קדוש, ובתחילת לידתו חולין הוה, ויכול למוכרו כאילו הוא במעי אמו, שהרי קדושתו תלוי בלידה; וכיון דמכירתו מכירה, ה"ל יד עובד כוכבים באמצע, ותו לא קדיש בב' שלישי אחרונים:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:13:1.english: From that point forward - From the emergence of the majority [of the fetus] and onward it is consecrated, and at the beginning of its birth it was non-sacred, so he can sell it just as if it were [still] in its mother's womb, since its consecration depends on birth; and since his sale is a [valid] sale, there is a gentile's hand [i.e., share] in it, and it is no longer consecrated in the last two-thirds:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:14:1.hebrew: יצא שליש דרך דופן - תחילה ע"י סם וסכין, ובגמר לידה נפתח רחם ויצאו שני שלישים:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:14:1.english: One-third emerged through the wall [of the womb] - First by means of a drug and a knife, and at the completion of birth the womb opened and two-thirds emerged:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:15:1.hebrew: למפרע הוא קדוש - הרוב הראשון קדושתו תלויה, שבתחלת לידה הוא צריך ליקדש:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:15:1.english: It is consecrated retroactively - The first majority — its sanctity depends [on it], for it must become consecrated at the beginning of birth:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:15:2.english: From that point forward - [it is consecrated] once its majority is born, whether at the beginning or at the end:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:16:1.english: For had we been taught [their dispute] in this [case] - [i.e.,] the first [case]:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:16:2.english: In this [case] Rav Huna says - [that] it is consecrated retroactively:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:16:3.hebrew: משום דלקולא - כלומר, דאי אמר "מכאן ולהבא", קולא הוא, דמפקעינן לבכור מקדושתו:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:16:3.english: Because [it is] a leniency - That is to say, if one says [that it is consecrated] from here onward, it is a leniency, for we [thereby] remove the firstborn from its sanctity:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:1:1.hebrew: בעינא פרסות - בבהמה, דהכי משמע: שתי פרסות ומעלת גרה הנמצאת בבהמה תאכלו:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:1:1.english: I require hooves - in the animal, for this is what [the verse] implies: [a creature with] "two hooves and chews the cud" that is found "in the animal — you may eat":

Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:1.hebrew: קלוט במעי פרה ליתסר - ואנן אמרינן לעיל (חולין דף סח:), דשרי אפי' לר"ש:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:1.english: [A fetus with] non-cloven [hooves] inside a cow’s womb should be forbidden - Yet we said above (Chullin 68b) that it is permitted even according to Rabbi Shimon:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:2.hebrew: תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל כר"ש - מצינו משנת מדרשו של ר' ישמעאל כתלמידיו של ר"ש בן יוחי:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:2.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - We find [that] the teaching of the study house of Rabbi Yishmael [is] like [that of] the disciples of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:3.hebrew: פרסה בבהמה תאכלו - קרא כתיב "פרסה" וכתיב "פרסות", איזה שתמצא: או פרסה בבהמה או פרסות; אבל יונה אינה לא פרסה ולא פרסות:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:2:3.english: A hoof, in the animal, you may eat - The verse writes "hoof" and writes "hooves" — whichever you find: either a [non-cloven] hoof in the animal, or [cloven] hooves; however, a dove[-shaped fetus] has neither a [non-cloven] hoof nor [cloven] hooves:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:3:1.english: As we said initially - that a fetus is called an "animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69b:3:2.hebrew: ר"ש היא - טעמא לאו משום דעובר לאו בהמה, אלא משום דמקיש תמורה למעשר במסכת תמורה בפ"ק, דתנן: אמר ר"ש: והלא מעשר בכלל כל הקדשים היה, ולמה יצא — דכתיב "כל מעשר בקר וצאן וגו' לא יבקר בין טוב לרע ולא ימירנו", ולמה יצא? להקיש: מה מעשר קרבן יחיד — יצא קרבן צבור, ומה מעשר קדשי מזבח — יצאו קדשי בדק הבית. הלכך דוק מינה נמי: מה מעשר אינו בעוברין ואברין, דבעינן "יעבור תחת השבט" (ויקרא כז):
Rashi on Chullin 69b:3:2.english: [It is the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon - The reason [one cannot substitute for a fetus] is not because a fetus is not [considered] an animal, but rather because he compares substitution to the [animal] tithe in tractate Temurah in the first chapter, as we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Shimon said: Was not the [animal] tithe already included in the general category of all consecrated animals? Why then was it singled out — as it is written, "All tithes of cattle and flock, etc. ... he shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it" [Leviticus 27:32–33] — why was it singled out? To establish a comparison: just as the [animal] tithe is an individual's offering, communal offerings are excluded; and just as the [animal] tithe is [among] offerings consecrated for the altar, items consecrated for Temple upkeep are excluded. Therefore, infer from it also: just as the [animal] tithe does not apply to fetuses and limbs — since we require [that it] "shall pass under the rod" (Leviticus 27[:32]) [so too, substitution does not apply to them]:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:3:3.hebrew: אף תמורה - אבל למאן דלא מקיש, ממירין, דעובר איקרי בהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:3:3.english: So too, substitution - However, according to the one who does not compare [substitution to the animal tithe], one may substitute [for a fetus], because a fetus is called an "animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69b:4:1.hebrew: ומנא תימרא - דהא "אין ממירין", ר"ש היא:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:4:1.english: And from where do you say - that this [statement,] "they do not effect substitution," is [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:4:2.hebrew: דתנן - בסיפא דידה, דפליג ר' יוסי עלה ואמר ממירין, ומפרש טעמא: "והלא במוקדשין" — בתחלת הקדש — "האומר רגלה של זו עולה, כולה עולה כו'". שמע מינה מדקאמר "והלא במוקדשין", דלרבי שמעון מהדר: "והלא במוקדשין אתה מודה דהאומר רגלה של זו כו' — כדלקמן — ובזו אתה חלוק עלי!". דאי ס"ד ת"ק דאמר "אין ממירים", ר"מ היא כשאר סתם משנה:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:4:2.english: As we learned [in the Mishnah] - In its latter clause, where Rabbi Yosei disagrees with it and says [that] they do effect substitution, and he explains the reason: "But with regard to consecrated [offerings]" — [meaning] in the initial consecration — "[if] one says, 'The leg of this [animal] is a burnt offering,' all of it is a burnt offering," etc. Learn from this, since he says "But with regard to consecrated [offerings]," that he is responding to Rabbi Shimon: "But with regard to consecrated [offerings] you agree that [if] one says, 'The leg of this [animal],' etc. — as [stated] below — yet in this [case] you disagree with me!" For if it should enter your mind that the Tanna Kamma [who says] "they do not effect substitution" is Rabbi Meir, like other anonymous Mishnahs:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:5:1.hebrew: מי אית להו האי סברא - במוקדשין דכולה עולה, דנימא להו רבי יוסי: "והלא במוקדשין אתם מודים לי"? והתניא כו':
Rashi on Chullin 69b:5:1.english: Do they accept this reasoning - regarding consecrated animals, that all of it [becomes] a burnt offering, such that Rabbi Yosei could say to them, "Do you not agree with me regarding consecrated animals?" But isn't it taught [in a baraita], etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:6:1.english: One might [have thought] it goes out to non-sacred [status] - through redemption, [meaning] that one redeems that limb:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:6:2.hebrew: תמכר - בהמה זו לצרכי עולות, ודמיה חולין:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:6:2.english: It shall be sold - This animal [shall be sold] for the needs of burnt offerings, and its proceeds [are] non-sacred:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:6:3.hebrew: חוץ מדמי אותו אבר - וממנו לא יטול הדמים, לפי שאינו שלו. ובתמורה פריך: והא קמייתי אותו שקנאה עולה מחוסר אבר, והוא היה מחוייב עולה:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:6:3.english: Except for the payment for that limb - And for it he does not take the payment, because it is not his. And in [Tractate] Temurah, [the Gemara] asks: Is the one who bought it not bringing a burnt offering that is lacking a limb, whereas he was obligated [to bring a whole] burnt offering?

Rashi on Chullin 69b:7:1.hebrew: יהיה לרבות את כולה - דה"ל למיכתב "כל אשר יתן ממנו לה' קדש", ומדכתיב "יהיה", ריבויא הוא, דאפי' לא נתן לה' אלא ממנו, דהיינו מקצתה, יהיה קדש כולה:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:7:1.english: "It shall be" [serves] to include all of it - For [Scripture] should have written: "all that one gives of it to the Lord [is] holy," and since it is written "it shall be," it is an inclusion — [meaning] that even if one gave to the Lord only "of it," that is, a part of it, all of it shall be holy.

Rashi on Chullin 69b:8:1.hebrew: אלא לאו - ת"ק ר"ש היא, וכיון דשמעת ליה בעלמא דמקיש תמורה למעשר, טעמא בהא נמי משום הקישא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:8:1.english: Rather, is it not [to Rabbi Shimon] - [Meaning] the Tanna Kamma is Rabbi Shimon; and since you have heard him [state] elsewhere that he compares temurah [an animal designated as a substitute for a sacrifice] to ma'aser [animal tithe], the reason here too is because of that scriptural analogy [hekesh]:

Rashi on Chullin 69b:9:1.hebrew: לא ר' יוסי טעמא דנפשיה קאמר - מהא לא תימא דת"ק ר"ש היא, דלעולם אימא לך דר"מ היא או ר' יהודה, דלא שמעינן להו דמקשו, וטעמייהו בהא משום דאברים ועוברין לאו בהמה מיקרו. ודקשיא לך: היכי מצי ר' יוסי למימר לר' מאיר "והלא במוקדשים כו'"? לאו משום דסבירא ליה דנימא "והלא במוקדשים אתה מודה לי", אלא ה"ק ליה: הלא במוקדשין יודע אני דהאומר "רגלה של זו עולה", כולה עולה, דנפקא ליה מ"יהיה קדש"; אף כשיאמר "רגלה של זו תמורה", תהא כולה תמורה, ואישתכח דהמיר בהמה כולה וקרינא בהמה בבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 69b:9:1.english: No, Rabbi Yosei stated his own reasoning - From this, do not say that the Tanna Kamma is Rabbi Shimon, for in fact I can tell you that it is Rabbi Meir or Rabbi Yehudah, for we have not heard them to make [that] comparison, and their reasoning in this [matter] is because limbs and fetuses are not called "an animal." And as for what was difficult for you: how could Rabbi Yosei say to Rabbi Meir, "Is it not so with consecrated animals, etc."? It is not because he holds [that he can] say, "Do you not agree with me regarding consecrated animals?" Rather, this is what he is saying to him: "Regarding consecrated animals, I know that if one says, 'The foot of this [animal] is a burnt offering,' the entire [animal] becomes a burnt offering, as it is derived from [the verse], 'it shall be holy'; [so] too, when one says, 'The foot of this [animal] is a substitute,' let the entire [animal] become a substitute, and it thus turns out that he has substituted an entire animal, and we can apply [the phrase] 'an animal for an animal'!"

Tosafot on Chullin 69b:10:1.hebrew: יצא רובו הרי זה יקבר - אע"ג דתנן בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לב:) דב"ה מתירין למנות עובד כוכבים על הבכור, הכא מודו דאסור למכור לעובד כוכבים; דהא מוקמינן לה התם כר"ע, ושמעינן ליה לר"ע בפרק טבול יום (זבחים דף קג:) דאמר: "מדבריו למדנו שהשוחט את הבכור ונמצא טרפה שיאותו הכהנים בעורו" — משמע דבשר אסור בהנאה. והיינו טעמא: דהיכא דשרי לישראל, הוא דאיתקש לצבי ואיל, ושרי אפי' לעובדי כוכבים:
Tosafot on Chullin 69b:10:1.english: If a majority of it had emerged, it must be buried - Even though we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 32b) that Beit Hillel permit inviting a non-Jew to share in a firstborn, here they agree that it is forbidden to sell [it] to a non-Jew; for we establish that [Mishnah] there in accordance with R' Akiva, and we have heard [the opinion] of R' Akiva in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (Zevachim 103b) who says: "From his words we learn that if one slaughters a firstborn and it is found to be a tereifah, the priests may benefit from its hide" — implying that the meat is forbidden for benefit. And this is the reason: where it is permitted to an Israelite, it is compared to a gazelle and a hart, and [therefore] it is permitted even to non-Jews:

Tosafot on Chullin 69b:12:1.hebrew: רב הונא אמר קדוש קסבר למפרע הוא קדוש - הא דאמר רב יהודה בפ' כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות לה.) דמותר להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא לאויר העולם, ומפרש: גדיא באזניה, אימרא בשיפוותיה, אבל אימרא באזניה לא, דחיישינן כי חזי ליה לאזניה שמא יצא רוב הראש וחזר, אבל בגדי אין לחוש, דמתוך דאזניו גדולות דרכו לצאת במיעוט הראש — והיינו דלא כרב הונא, דלדידיה, כיון דלמפרע קדוש, אפי' לא יצא רוב הראש אסור להטיל בו מום, דכשיצא אח"כ הרוב איגלאי מילתא למפרע דקדוש הוה, כדאמרי' הכא גבי מכירה. ומיהו איכא לאוקמי האי דרב יהודה אליבא דרב הונא, ומכי חזי לאזנו דגדיא בפנים שרי להטיל בו מום, דאכתי לא יצא כלל, אבל אימרא איכא למיחש מכי חזי לאזניה בפנים שכבר יצא רוב הראש וחזר. וסוגיא דריש כיצד מערימין (תמורה דף כד:), דמוקי דרב יהודה בזמן הזה דלא חזי להקרבה, ופריך: מאי למימרא? ומשני: מהו דתימא נגזור אטו דלמא נפיק רוב הראש — ההיא סוגיא דלא כרב הונא, דלרב הונא במיעוט ראשו נמי איכא איסור. וכן הא דא"ל רב עמרם לרב ששת: אמר על הבכור "עם יציאת רובו יהא עולה", עולה הוא או בכור הוי? ההיא נמי דלא כרב הונא, דמשמע דפשיטא ליה דקודם יציאת רובו יכול להפקיע ממנו קדושת בכור — אם לא נחלק בין מכירה לעובד כוכבים להנך:
Tosafot on Chullin 69b:12:1.english: Rav Huna says it is consecrated, as he maintains it is consecrated retroactively - That which Rav Yehudah said in the chapter [entitled] Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 35a), that it is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it emerges into the air of the world — and [the Gemara there] explains: a kid on its ear, a lamb on its lips, but a lamb on its ear [is] not [permitted], because we are concerned when one sees its ear that perhaps most of the head emerged and went back [in], whereas with a kid there is no need to be concerned, because since its ears are large, it is its way to emerge [even] with a minority of the head [having emerged] — this is not in accordance with Rav Huna. For according to him, since it is consecrated retroactively, even if most of the head has not emerged, it is forbidden to inflict a blemish on it, because when the majority emerges afterward, it becomes clarified retroactively that it was consecrated, as we say here regarding a sale. However, it is possible to establish this [statement] of Rav Yehudah in accordance with Rav Huna, [meaning] that when one sees the ear of a kid inside [the womb], it is permitted to inflict a blemish on it, since it has not yet emerged at all; whereas [for] a lamb there is room to be concerned when one sees its ear inside that most of the head has already emerged and gone back [in]. And the sugya at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Ma'arimin (Temurah 24b), which establishes [the statement] of Rav Yehudah as [referring to] the present time, when it is not fit for sacrifice, and asks: "What need is there to state [this]?" and answers: "Lest you say we should decree [a prohibition] on account of [the possibility that] perhaps most of the head emerged" — that sugya is not in accordance with Rav Huna, for according to Rav Huna, there is a prohibition even with a minority of its head [having emerged]. And similarly, that which Rav Amram said to Rav Sheshet: [If one] said concerning a firstborn, "With the emergence of its majority, let it be a burnt offering," is it a burnt offering or is it a firstborn? — that [passage] too is not in accordance with Rav Huna, since it implies that it is obvious to him that before the emergence of its majority he can remove the sanctity of a firstborn from it — unless we distinguish between a sale to a gentile and these [cases]:

Tosafot on Chullin 69b:6:1.hebrew: תמכר לצרכי עולות - לא דמי לבהמה של ב' שותפים, והקדיש חציה וחזר ולקחה והקדיש חציה, דאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ז.) דקדושה ואינה קריבה, דחשיבה דחויה מעיקרא; דהתם לא הוה בידו להקדישה כולה מתחלה, אבל הכא כשהקדיש רגלה, היה יכול להקדישה כולה:
Tosafot on Chullin 69b:6:1.english: It shall be sold for the needs of burnt offerings - This is not comparable to [the case of] an animal belonging to two partners, where [one] consecrated half of it and then bought it and consecrated [the other] half of it — regarding which we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a) that it is consecrated yet cannot be offered, because it is considered rejected from the outset; for there, it was not in his power to consecrate all of it at the beginning, whereas here, when he consecrated its leg, he was able to consecrate all of it:
